annotations.text:
Journal — the chosen direction, filled out.

Newsreader for content, Instrument Sans for labels and numerals. Paper ground, hairline rules instead of cards, one deep-green accent. Nothing is a container: hierarchy comes from type size and rule weight.

The ink theme is the same screen recoloured, not a second design — the app already ships light / dark / AMOLED, so 'Black' in Settings still needs drawing.

Two things here are not in the app yet: the 'write a line about today' field at the bottom of the list, and the linked-agent row in Settings showing coaching as an in-app toggle rather than only a notification channel.
The four directions not taken, kept for reference. Each is one main screen and one detail screen, in English, with its own type voice: A Instrument Sans, B IBM Plex Sans, C Space Grotesk, E Figtree.

All six widget types the app already registers, in the Journal language: checkmark (2×2, plus its measurable variant), score, streak, frequency, target (4×2) and history (4×3).

The ring-and-glyph checkmark widget is the one thing that does not survive the direction — a ring is the wrong vocabulary next to hairline rules. Score moves to a filled rule along the bottom edge, which reads at a glance and matches the rest of the design.

The app already exposes a background-alpha setting, so the second panel shows the transparent state: no card, ink inverts, empty history cells go to translucent white so they hold up over an unknown wallpaper.

Stack widgets (swipe through several habits) reuse these frames unchanged and are not drawn separately.
